item.title: Antipodes Island Sees Ground Beetle Numbers Surge 40-Fold After Mice Eradication
item.description: The successful removal of invasive house mice from Antipodes Island has spurred a remarkable resurgence in ground beetle populations, which have increased to around 40 times their former numbers. This ecological transformation highlights the beneficial effects of eradicating invasive species, fostering a healthier food web and aiding in the survival of native bird species. Long-term observation is crucial for comprehending the recovery dynamics of island ecosystems. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.description: The US tech giant is investing $15bn in a huge new data centre project in northern Finland. Fuente: Al Jazeera English.

item.title: Texas’s Historic Imperial Sugar Char House Gets $15M Rescue After 20 Years Vacant
item.description: Sugar Land City Council has given a green light for a $15 million initiative to safeguard the iconic Imperial Sugar Char House. This undertaking aims to stabilize the structure and prevent further deterioration over the years ahead. Work is set to commence shortly, with an anticipated completion by 2028. Officials are still finalizing plans for potential future utilizations, leaving residents eager for tangible development on this cherished landmark. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Key Atlantic currents could collapse this century, but the risk is missing from almost all national climate plans
item.description: Icelandic government officials recently met to discuss a dramatic scenario: what if the current that circulates Atlantic waters weakened significantly, or collapsed altogether? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Famed oceanographer calls for ending krill catch near Antarctica as governments debate fishing quota
item.description: Renowned oceanographer Sylvia Earle is calling for an end to krill fishing near Antarctica as officials from the U.S., China, Russia and 24 other governments negotiate a possible deal to dramatically expand fishing for the crustacean that's a vital food source for whales in the international waters surrounding the ice-covered continent. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nighttime songs could reveal when endangered pygmy blue whales feed off Western Australia
item.description: Listening to the songs of endangered pygmy blue whales could help researchers identify when the animals are feeding off Western Australia's coast, improving scientists' ability to monitor their behavior and inform conservation efforts. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Deeply regressive': How the French government plans to make protesters pay for riots and looting
item.description: As France continues to pick up the pieces after riots and looting broke out on the fringes of nationwide peaceful demonstrations on October 17, the government is pushing forward a bill that would make protesters have to pay up to €10,000 in reparations for damage caused during public unrest – even if they were not directly responsible for the vandalism. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Hong Kong’s leader apologises for residential fire that killed 168 people
item.description: Blaze was world’s deadliest residential fire since 1980, but some survivors and bereaved families say justice has yet to be served Hong Kong’s leader has apologised for government shortcomings that contributed to a fire that killed 168 people in the city last year, a rare sign of public contrition that nevertheless failed to impress some victims’ families. The chief executive, John Lee, and seven other officials bowed in apology at the release of a report that pointed to “decades of failure” by government bodies. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Lt. Gen. Ben Hodges accuses Hegseth of 'getting rid of people who may have the courage to push back'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye welcomes Lt. General (ret.) Ben Hodges, former commander of US Army Europe and NATO Allied Land Command. The dismissal of senior military officers without public explanation raises fundamental questions about institutional trust and the relationship between civilian authority and military leadership. For General Hodges, the reported firing of Lt. General Brett Sylvia reflects a potentially troubling pattern within the Pentagon under Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Equally striking is his criticism of the reluctance of retired senior commanders to speak publicly against policies… Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Researchers create first whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate
item.description: Viewed from above, Danionella cerebrum offers a rare sight in a vertebrate: its brain, visible through the top of its head. Since the species was adopted for neuroscience research in 2018 and formally described in 2021, the tiny, transparent fish has drawn rapidly growing interest for its unique biology. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Birds and humans share fundamental song and speech patterns, study finds
item.description: McGill University researchers have identified "universal" vocal patterns across hundreds of bird species and found that many of the same patterns also appear in human song and speech from cultures around the world. The patterns include small pitch intervals, regular and predictable rhythms, and phrase-final elongation, in which the last utterance in a phrase tends to be longer than the others. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chessum signs new two-year deal with Leicester
item.description: Leicester Tigers captain Ollie Chessum has signed a new multi-year deal to stay at Welford Road. Fuente: BBC Sport.

item.title: Long-distance flights can throw seabirds' internal clocks out of sync, causing navigation errors
item.description: A study led by Oxford University has found that seabirds flying long distances across the Atlantic can experience a mismatch between their internal body clocks and local time (the same process that leads to jet lag in humans), causing them to make predictable errors when navigating by the sun. The results have been published in the journal Science. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Names Troy Asher Armstrong Flight Research Center Director
item.description: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman has named Troy Asher director of the agency’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California. Asher, a veteran test pilot and aerospace engineer with decades of experience in flight research and operations, has served as the center’s acting director since March. “Troy has spent his career pushing the boundaries of flight, […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Analysis of Córdoba's urban trees identifies which species best tolerate heat
item.description: The orange tree emerges as one of the most heat-vulnerable trees, according to a University of Córdoba (UCO) study that analyzed 17 tree species found in Córdoba's urban environment. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why jet lag throws even foraging seabirds off course
item.description: Oxford study shows Manx shearwaters lose direction when their body clocks get out of sync Seabirds returning from foraging trips can be thrown hundreds of miles off course by a form of jet lag that arises when their body clocks get out of sync with local time, researchers say. Tracking data from Manx shearwaters on the west coast of the UK revealed that when the birds returned home to their colonies after trips over the Atlantic, their rapid eastward flights disrupted their sense of time and navigation. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.
item.dc:creator: Hanad Ahmed

item.title: Global maps reveal farming, dams and agricultural runoff as leading threats to freshwater species
item.description: Farming, dams and agricultural runoff are the biggest threats to freshwater biodiversity globally, with Europe and Northwest Africa the hardest-hit regions, McGill researchers have found. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI helps uncover overlooked 2D materials and create 11 new ones
item.description: With the help of artificial intelligence, researchers at Linköping University in Sweden have found previously overlooked occurrences of the 2D materials MXenes in older databases. The findings have inspired the researchers to create new materials using more sustainable synthesis methods. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: One molecule, many atoms: Platinum bonds respond to surface features up to 10 nanometers away
item.description: Many chemical processes that sustain modern society depend on molecules binding to metal surfaces. The production of synthetic fertilizer, for example, relies on heterogeneous catalysis, in which gases react on the surface of a solid catalyst. Yet, until now, an important question has remained unresolved: How much of the metal surface actually participates in determining the strength of a chemical bond on the surface? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Economist delivers 'worst-case scenario' on interest rates as inflation fails to cool
item.description: The Reserve Bank has so far been unable to pull inflation down to its target range of between 2 and 3 per cent. The only option left, it seems, is to take a sledgehammer to demand. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
